cluster_lifecycle.query: TKE cluster creation provisioning upgrades node management auto-repair SLA availability
cluster_lifecycle.content:
# TKE Cluster Management: Key Documentation Facts

## Facts

- **Node Pool Management**: TKE supports basic node pool features for convenient creation, management, and termination of nodes with dynamic scaling capabilities[1]. Node pools allow you to upgrade both Kubernetes and Docker versions[1] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35900)

- **Auto Scaling Configuration**: Node pools support auto scaling that automatically adjusts node quantity based on cluster workload[1]. Manual node quantity adjustment is also available as an alternative[1] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35900)

- **Rapid Scaling Implementation**: TKE provides `tke-autoscaling-placeholder` tool enabling scaling in seconds using low-priority placeholder pods (default 10 replicas, 300m CPU per replica) that reserve buffer resources for high-priority workloads during traffic spikes[2] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/38856)

- **Node Pool Modifications**: You can modify node pool name, operating system, node quantity in scaling groups, and Kubernetes labels/taints; label and taint modifications affect all nodes and may trigger pod rescheduling[1] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35903)

- **Kubernetes Version Support Lifecycle**: TKE maintains four support stages—GA (General Availability), EOM (End of Marketing at 18 months), EOFS (End of Full Support at 24 months), and EOS (End of Service at 27 months)[6]. Current supported versions include 1.34 (GA: November 25, 2025), 1.32, 1.30, 1.28, 1.26, 1.24, 1.22, and 1.20[6] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/47894)

- **Node Scale-in Behavior**: During auto scaling, nodes are marked unschedulable, pods are drained/deleted, then the node is released[1]. Scale-in evaluation typically occurs within minutes depending on configuration[5] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35900)

- **Audit and Troubleshooting**: TKE provides audit logs and event services for troubleshooting cluster issues, including tracking cluster-autoscaler events and node health problems[4] (URL: https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/38937)

## Key URLs

- https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35900: Node Pool Overview and auto scaling configuration
- https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/38856: Rapid auto scaling with tke-autoscaling-placeholder
- https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/47894: Kubernetes version maintenance and support lifecycle
- https://www.tencentcloud.com/document/product/457/35903: Node pool adjustment procedures

**Note**: [UNVERIFIED] Specific SLA availability percentages and cluster creation provisioning timelines are not detailed in the provided documentation.
